column1: # Hand-verified English↔Idoma evaluation seed
# Format:  english <TAB> idoma <TAB> dialect (optional: central|western|"")
# Lines starting with '#' are comments. build_corpus.py forces every pair here
# into the TEST split and removes any matching English key from train/dev, so
# these are a clean held-out set.
# RULE: only add a pair you have actually verified.
# The reason this file starts nearly empty is deliberate. The project's previous
# dataset (backend/idoma_dictionary_v2.json) was filled with invented entries and
# that is what broke it: 109 of 218 rows were the placeholder "ụụ", and among the
# 107 that survived filtering, "òdò" was given as the translation of black, day,
# evening, morning, night AND red, and "ófé" as both "Please" and "Thank you".
# A wrong evaluation set is worse than a small one: it makes a broken model look
# fine. So this file only contains pairs read off a citable source or confirmed by
# a speaker.
# Where to get more:
#   1. https://www.scribd.com/document/1006452998/English-Idoma-Wordlist
#      ~74 tone-marked pairs. The page is behind a bot wall, so it cannot be
#      scraped — open it in a browser and copy the pairs in by hand.
#   2. https://www.idomaland.org/dictionary
#      Scraped automatically by scrape_idomaland.py. Do NOT copy rows from the
#      scrape into this file: the point of this set is to be independent of it.
#   3. A native speaker reviewing candidate rows.
# Target: ~60 pairs. Mix single words with short phrases, and note the dialect
# when the source does, because central and western Idoma differ (water is Ennkpo
# in central and Enyi in western).
# Smoke-test pairs, NOT independent evaluation (2026-09-02)
# These five were read off live idomaland.org pages by hand, so they share a
# source with the training corpus and break the independence rule above. They are
# kept anyway for one narrow purpose: each has two dialect forms or an apostrophe,
# so they exercise the multi-reference and diacritic paths in the notebook's
# scoring cell. Do not read a score on these as evidence of generalisation, and
# do not add more of them — everything below the last divider should come from
# Scribd or a speaker.
water
water
eat
eat
I am singing
